## Description
&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;Fiberglass-epoxy composite (commonly known by its NEMA grade designation FR-4) &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;is a layered laminate made from two core materials:&#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;1. Woven E-glass fiberglass cloth — provides mechanical strength, rigidity, and dimensional &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;   stability.  The glass fibers are non-conductive, moisture-resistant, and chemically inert.&#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;2. Epoxy resin — a thermosetting polymer that cures under heat and pressure, binding the &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;   glass layers together and providing electrical insulation, chemical resistance, and &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;   thermal durability.  Flame-retardant additives (typically brominated compounds) are &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;   mixed into the resin to give the material its self-extinguishing (UL 94 V-0) property. &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;   &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;By weight, a typical FR-4 laminate is roughly 60% glass fiber / 40% epoxy resin.  &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;In PCB fabrication, copper foil is laminated to one or both faces of the FR-4 core, then &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;etched to form the conductive traces. &#10;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;The name breaks down as: FR &#61; Flame Retardant, 4 &#61; the NEMA material class code indicating &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;epoxy resin + glass cloth reinforcement at the UL 94 V-0 fire rating.  &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;&#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;It&#39;s the standard substrate for the vast majority of rigid printed circuit boards, &#10;&#9;&#9;&#9;including the green board inside a RAM module. &#9;&#9;&#9;&#9;   &#10;&#9;&#9;
